content.text: {"primary_meaning":"The Holy Spirit—especially divine anointing, consecration, presence, and empowerment for service—is the symbolic meaning most commonly assigned to oil in Christian teaching.","primary_basis":["1 Samuel 16:13 — David is anointed with oil, and the Spirit of the LORD comes powerfully upon him.","Isaiah 61:1 and Luke 4:18 — anointing is associated with the Spirit resting upon and commissioning the Messiah.","Acts 10:38 — God anoints Jesus with the Holy Spirit and power.","Zechariah 4:1-14, especially 4:6 — the vision of the oil-fed lampstand is explained in terms of God's Spirit rather than human might.","2 Corinthians 1:21-22 — divine anointing is linked with the Spirit given as a guarantee.","1 John 2:20, 27 — believers receive an 'anointing,' commonly interpreted in Christian teaching as the Holy Spirit."] ,"alternatives":[{"meaning":"Consecration, appointment, or authorization for a sacred office, particularly that of priest, king, prophet, or Messiah. This may overlap with Spirit symbolism but can function independently as a ritual and vocational sign.","basis":["Exodus 28:41; 29:7","Exodus 30:22-33","Leviticus 8:10-12","1 Samuel 10:1","1 Kings 19:15-16","Psalm 2:2"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Healing or medicinal care, sometimes accompanied by prayer and divine healing rather than functioning as a direct symbol of the Holy Spirit.","basis":["Isaiah 1:6","Mark 6:13","Luke 10:34","James 5:14"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Joy, honor, refreshment, blessing, prosperity, or festal abundance.","basis":["Psalm 23:5","Psalm 45:7","Psalm 104:15","Isaiah 61:3","Ecclesiastes 9:8","Hebrews 1:9"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Light, spiritual readiness, vigilance, or persevering preparedness, especially through oil used in lamps.","basis":["Exodus 27:20-21","Matthew 25:1-13"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Hospitality, personal honor, grooming, or mourning practices, often reflecting ordinary ancient custom rather than a fixed theological symbol.","basis":["2 Samuel 14:2","Psalm 23:5","Matthew 6:17","Luke 7:46"],"prominence":"minority"},{"meaning":"Oil as an ordinary commodity—food, fuel, medicine, trade goods, or agricultural produce—with no necessary symbolic meaning in a given passage.","basis":["Deuteronomy 7:13","1 Kings 17:12-16","2 Kings 4:1-7","Luke 16:6","Revelation 6:6"],"prominence":"common"}],"has_settled_consensus":false,"confidence":"high","notes":"There is a recognizable dominant Christian convention identifying oil with the Holy Spirit, particularly where anointing and empowerment occur together. Nevertheless, biblical interpretation does not treat oil as a universal one-to-one symbol. Its meaning is strongly context-dependent, and many passages concern consecration, healing, joy, hospitality, lamp fuel, or ordinary material use instead."}
